dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Read graph headers, checked node/edge sizes via wc, and explicitly noted node-name conventions per network (DM/HS numeric IDs, Y2K gene names, SC numeric IDs) — characterizing both pairs' format and sizes.
Inspected the reference alignment, observed 2379 lines == Yeast2KReduced node count, and exploited it directly (cp for NC=1.0) — recognizing the key task-specific NC lever.

Enumerated multiple known alignment approaches (degree-sort, GRAAL/MAGNA, seed-and-extend, SANA) with rationale and computed a baseline degree-sorted S3=0.01, distinguishing the two deliverables' differing needs (reference-exploit vs topology).
No further orientation — the remainder is terminal-freeze troubleshooting; no degree-distribution analysis or external literature research ever occurs.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and selects known-reasonable methods with stated rationale — clearing anchor 5. It goes further by noticing task-specific levers (reference-exploit for NC, topology for S3) and the differing per-deliverable constraints, and by computing a baseline score, pushing toward 6-7. But it never systematically characterizes degree distributions or conducts genuine research/fit analysis of published methods (methods are recalled, not researched), so it stops short of anchor 8. Level 6.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones

evidence.note: Recognized the two deliverables as distinct: exploited the perfect reference for yeast (NC=1.0 by direct copy) and identified fly as needing a real S3>=0.32 alignment — tracking both deliverables and their thresholds distinctly, and effectively budgeting effort by difficulty.
Separated stages: parsed graphs, built a scorer, and computed a degree-sorted baseline (S3=0.01) before writing the SANA optimizer — scorer/baseline built before optimizing against it.
Ran with a short time limit to gauge speed and detected the optimizer was degrading S3, showing score-tied checks on the optimize stage.
Terminal froze and the remainder of the trajectory was consumed by repeated unfreeze attempts with no milestone structure, so the decomposition discipline was confined to the first ~16 steps.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly separated parsing, scoring, baseline generation, and optimization, and handled the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals — meeting the level-5 anchor — while also sequencing sensibly (scorer/baseline before optimizer) and implicitly budgeting effort by difficulty (perfect-ref yeast vs S3-only fly), pushing toward level 8. It falls short of 8 because milestones were never explicitly enumerated with numeric done-criteria or fallback branches, and the sequencing was implicit rather than a stated milestone hierarchy. Level 6 reflects solid stage separation with sensible, partly score-gated ordering but no explicit milestone framework.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: Wrote align.py/sana.py that compute S3 and report its components (Ea=1399, E1=34753, E2a=101586, S3=0.01), matching the spec formula including the E2_aligned denominator — a faithful S3 implementation used to measure the baseline.
Monitored S3 across simulated-annealing iterations (noticed S3 going DOWN, acc≈iters) and tuned temperature accordingly, using the S3 score as the optimization signal.

For y2kr-SC only checked coverage via line count (wc -l = 2379 = num nodes) and copied the reference for assumed NC=1.0; never implemented an NC scorer or validated injectivity / exact node-name-format matching.
After the terminal broke, all verification collapsed; agent submitted DM-HS blind, explicitly unable to confirm its S3, so no passing local score was ever confirmed for that deliverable.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built and ran a faithful S3 implementation and used it as the optimization objective (above the level-3 'rough proxy' anchor), but it never implemented NC (relied on copying the reference for assumed NC=1.0) and never performed injectivity, full-coverage, or exact node-name/format validation beyond line counts — falling short of the level-5 anchor's requirement for S3+NC plus injectivity/coverage/format checks. No sanity-checking of the scorer against the reference (level 8) occurred, and verification broke down entirely at the end. This places the behavior between anchors 3 and 5, closer to 5 on the S3 side, so a 4.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: Computed and reported initial degree-sorted S3 = 0.01 and compared it against the 0.32 target, establishing current-score-vs-threshold awareness.
Detected a regression ('S3 is going DOWN', 'acc ≈ iters'), reported Ea/E1/E2a internals, and diagnosed the acceptance-probability bug — genuine trend/regression monitoring.

Knew which deliverable still fell short: y2kr-SC solved via perfect reference (NC=1.0), DM-HS remaining and last known at S3≈0.0006 — but no best-so-far was preserved; the good/bad alignment file distinction was never protected.
After terminal broke, the agent had zero score visibility for the entire rest of the run; no logging, no best-so-far, and it submitted blind, acknowledging it could not verify DM-HS quality.

dimensions.reasoning: Early in the run the agent tracked current S3 against the 0.32 threshold, reported the underlying edge counts, knew which deliverable still fell short, and even detected a regression — behavior consistent with anchor 5 and briefly touching the regression-recognition of anchor 8. However, it never maintained a best-so-far or preserved the best alignment, and monitoring vanished entirely for the majority of the horizon after the terminal broke, so it clearly does not reach 8/10. The mix of solid early threshold/regression awareness with a total loss of continuity across the run places it at a 4.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: Recognized that y2kr-SC has a perfect reference alignment and used it directly to satisfy the NC constraint (NC=1.0) — an appropriate, signal-aware choice exploiting reference seeding rather than grinding topology for that deliverable.

Degree-sorted baseline gave S3≈0.01; agent recognized this was far below target and switched to a materially different tactic (SANA simulated-annealing local search) prompted by the observed shortfall — clears the level-5 bar.

Diagnosed WHY the SA run failed (nearly all moves accepted, S3 decreasing because delta/T made exp(delta/T)≈1) and deliberately pivoted by lowering T_start/T_end — genuine root-cause diagnosis and targeted correction (level-8 flavor).

From step ~19 onward the trajectory is dominated by a frozen terminal; the agent made no further algorithmic adaptation, never confirmed or improved the DM-HS S3, and ultimately submitted a below-threshold DM-HS file. The adaptation arc was truncated by the environment, not extended into fluid multi-hypothesis course-correction.

dimensions.reasoning: In the working window the agent showed real adaptive behavior: it abandoned a failing degree-sort baseline for SANA (level 5), correctly diagnosed the simulated-annealing acceptance bug and tuned temperature deliberately (level-8 diagnostic pivot), and chose reference seeding for the NC-constrained deliverable. However, only one or two adaptation cycles actually occurred before a terminal freeze derailed the rest of the run, so we never observe the sustained, multi-hypothesis, dead-end-abandoning fluidity of levels 8-10. This places observed behavior between the level-5 'materially different tactic' and level-8 'diagnose-and-pivot' anchors, landing at 6.

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
